title: DFS in Reykjavík: Find Paths Like a Depth Diver
description: Watch DFS explore Reykjavík’s street network by going deep before it backtracks. Can you spot how the traversal order shapes the route outcome?
ig_caption:
🌍✨ Reykjavík (Miðborg) Street Map + DFS Visualization!

In this reel, DFS (Depth-First Search) tackles a real-world pathfinding problem by treating the street grid as a graph 🕸️: intersections become nodes and street segments become edges. Rather than expanding level-by-level like BFS, DFS dives down one path as far as possible, then backtracks when it hits dead ends 🔁—the classic “go deep, then retrace” behavior.

🧠 Graph theory angle: DFS runs along adjacency lists, maintaining a visited set to avoid cycles, which is crucial on dense street maps where loops are everywhere. Because DFS prioritizes depth over distance, the path you see can differ dramatically from the shortest route—but it reveals how traversal order explores connectivity.
